title: DMM reading-plus-range accuracy bound
description: Convert a manufacturer's DC voltage accuracy specification into separate gain and range contributions and a worst-case reading interval.
formula: E_read = abs(V_read) a/100; E_range = V_range b/100; E = E_read + E_range; V_low,high = V_read +/- E
assumptions: The specification uses percent of reading plus percent of the selected positive full-scale range, not percent of the bipolar span or display counts.
The stated coefficients apply at the actual temperature, calibration age, integration setting and measurement function. Additional specified errors must already be accounted for.
The interval is a specification error bound, not a confidence interval or standard uncertainty. Loading and lead errors are excluded.

references.title: Keithley E-Handbook to Understanding Electrical Test and Measurement, Step 2: Accuracy and Instrumentation error

constraints.message: Reading must lie within the selected full-scale range; overrange specifications are outside this model

title: Three-point delta resistance and thermal-EMF rejection
description: Recover resistance from equally spaced +I, -I, +I four-wire readings while canceling constant and linearly drifting thermoelectric voltage.
formula: V_R = (V1-2 V2+V3)/4; R = V_R/I; E_mid = (V1+2 V2+V3)/4; dE/dt = (V3-V1)/(2 delta_t)
assumptions: The three readings are equally spaced by delta_t, at settled currents +I, -I, +I of equal magnitude. Voltage lead polarity does not reverse.
DUT is an ohmic, nonnegative resistance with negligible change from self-heating during the cycle; four-wire sensing excludes force-lead drops.
Thermoelectric EMF is linear over the cycle. Quadratic drift, current mismatch, unsettled switching transients and voltage noise are not canceled.

references.title: Keithley Low-Voltage Measurement Techniques, The Delta Method of Measuring Resistance and Equipment Requirements

constraints.message: Readings must imply a nonnegative ohmic resistance with the stated voltage polarity
